obligations.provision: Schedule 1, APP 1.1–1.6
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Sch 1, Part 1, clauses 1.1–1.6 (APP 1)
obligations.title: Open and accountable management of personal information
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APP entity must take reasonable steps to implement practices, procedures and systems that ensure compliance with the Australian Privacy Principles and enable handling of privacy inquiries and complaints, and must maintain a clearly expressed and up-to-date APP privacy policy.
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APP entity under Privacy Act 1988 s 6C
AI system collects, holds, uses or discloses personal information
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All Australian banks (ADIs) and APP entities operating AI workflows handling personal information.
obligations.control_objective: Maintain accountable privacy governance and practices for the AI use case.

suggested_questions.privacy_accountability_assigned: Has an accountable privacy owner been assigned for this AI use case?
suggested_questions.privacy_practices_implemented: Has the bank documented and implemented the privacy practices required for this AI use case?
suggested_questions.privacy_policy_current: Does the current privacy policy accurately describe the bank's handling of personal information relevant to this AI use case?

obligations.source_location: Schedule 1, Part 1 — Consideration of personal information privacy
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Reasonable steps under APP 1.2 depend on the sensitivity, volume and risk profile of the AI use case.

obligations.provision: Schedule 1, APP 3.1–3.6
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Sch 1, Part 2, clauses 3.1–3.6 (APP 3)
obligations.title: Collection of solicited personal information
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An organisation must not collect personal information unless reasonably necessary for one or more of its functions or activities, must collect only by lawful and fair means directly from the individual unless unreasonable or impracticable, and must obtain consent before collecting sensitive information unless an exception applies.
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APP entity
AI system ingests, prompts for, scrapes or solicits personal or sensitive information
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: APP entities collecting customer, employee or third-party personal information for AI training, fine-tuning, RAG or inference.
obligations.control_objective: Limit collection to information reasonably necessary for the function and obtain consent where required.

suggested_questions.collection_purpose_defined: Is each category of personal information collected by the AI system linked to a documented business purpose?
suggested_questions.necessity_assessed: Has the bank verified that each collected personal-information field is reasonably necessary for that purpose?
suggested_questions.sensitive_information_consent: Where sensitive information is collected, is the required consent or other lawful basis documented?

obligations.source_location: Schedule 1, Part 2 — Collection of personal information
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Whether inferred attributes generated by an AI model constitute 'collection' of solicited/unsolicited personal information under APP 3/4 requires legal review.

obligations.provision: Schedule 1, APP 5.1–5.2
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Sch 1, Part 2, clauses 5.1–5.2 (APP 5)
obligations.title: Notification of collection
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: At or before the time an APP entity collects personal information about an individual (or if not practicable, as soon as practicable after), it must take reasonable steps to notify the individual of prescribed matters including collection purposes, consequences of non-collection, usual disclosures and overseas disclosures.
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APP entity
AI workflow collects personal information from or about individuals
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: Customer-facing and internal banking AI touchpoints collecting personal information.
obligations.control_objective: Provide required collection notices at or before collection, or as soon as practicable.

suggested_questions.collection_notice_exists: Is a privacy collection notice presented wherever the AI use case collects personal information?
suggested_questions.notice_content_complete: Does the notice include the required purposes, disclosures, access and complaint information?
suggested_questions.notice_timing_defined: Is the notice provided at or before collection, or as soon as practicable afterward?

obligations.source_location: Schedule 1, Part 2 — Notification of the collection of personal information
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: None; statutory notice elements in APP 5.2(a)-(j) are explicit.

obligations.provision: Schedule 1, APP 6.1–6.3
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Sch 1, Part 3, clauses 6.1–6.3 (APP 6)
obligations.title: Use or disclosure of personal information
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: Personal information held for a primary purpose must not be used or disclosed for a secondary purpose unless the individual has consented, the secondary purpose is related (or directly related for sensitive information) and within reasonable expectations, or another statutory exception applies.
applicability_conditions: Entity holds personal information
AI system uses personal information for model training, testing, prompting or disclosure
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All banking AI use cases repurposing customer transaction, interaction or credit records.
obligations.control_objective: Constrain personal-information use and disclosure to permitted purposes.

suggested_questions.primary_purpose_recorded: Is the primary purpose for each use of personal information by the AI system documented?
suggested_questions.secondary_use_basis_checked: Does every secondary use or disclosure have documented consent, reasonable expectation or another permitted basis?
suggested_questions.disclosures_logged: Are external and internal disclosures by the AI workflow recorded and reviewable?

obligations.source_location: Schedule 1, Part 3 — Dealing with personal information
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Using production customer data for secondary AI model training or fine-tuning requires case-by-case APP 6.2(a) reasonable-expectation or consent analysis.

obligations.provision: Schedule 1, APP 8.1–8.2; s 16C
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) s 16C and Sch 1, Part 3, clauses 8.1–8.2 (APP 8)
obligations.title: Cross-border disclosure of personal information
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: Before disclosing personal information to an overseas recipient (such as an offshore cloud AI model provider or foreign support team), an APP entity must take reasonable steps to ensure the overseas recipient does not breach the APPs and remains accountable under s 16C unless an APP 8.2 exception applies.
applicability_conditions: AI workflow handles personal information
Personal information is transmitted to, accessed from, or inferenced in an overseas jurisdiction
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: Banking AI systems using cross-border LLM APIs, global cloud regions or offshore subcontractors.
obligations.control_objective: Assess overseas data flows and enforce APP 8 / s 16C cross-border privacy protections before offshore AI processing.

suggested_questions.overseas_recipients_and_regions_mapped: Are all countries, cloud regions and overseas recipients that can access personal information in the AI workflow mapped?
suggested_questions.app8_reasonable_steps_and_contracts_in_p: Are binding contractual and technical controls in place to ensure any overseas AI recipient complies with the APPs?
suggested_questions.s16c_accountability_and_exception_assess: Has Legal assessed whether transfers constitute a disclosure vs. limited use and confirmed s 16C accountability or an APP 8.2 exception?

obligations.source_location: Section 16C & Schedule 1, Part 3 — Cross-border disclosure of personal information
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Distinguishing 'use' (where the bank retains strict technical control over offshore infrastructure) from 'disclosure' under OAIC Chapter 8 v1.3 guidelines requires fact-specific legal review.

obligations.provision: Schedule 1, APP 10.1–10.2
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Sch 1, Part 4, clauses 10.1–10.2 (APP 10)
obligations.title: Quality of personal information collected, used or disclosed
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APP entity must take reasonable steps to ensure personal information it collects is accurate, up-to-date and complete (APP 10.1), and that personal information it uses or discloses is, having regard to the purpose of the use or disclosure, accurate, up-to-date, complete and relevant (APP 10.2).
applicability_conditions: AI workflow collects, uses, infers or discloses personal information about individuals
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: Banking AI systems generating customer summaries, risk scores, eligibility assessments or automated correspondence.
obligations.control_objective: Ensure personal information and AI-generated inferences about individuals are accurate, complete, up-to-date and relevant for the decision purpose.

suggested_questions.input_personal_data_accuracy_checked: What controls verify that customer personal information fed into the AI system is accurate, complete and up-to-date?
suggested_questions.ai_output_and_inference_relevance_verifi: How does the bank prevent inaccurate or hallucinated AI outputs about a customer from being used or disclosed?
suggested_questions.stale_or_incomplete_records_prevented: Are automated checks in place to reject stale or incomplete customer records before AI inference?

obligations.source_location: Schedule 1, Part 4 — Integrity of personal information
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Application of APP 10.2 to probabilistic generative AI summaries requires thresholds aligned to the consequence of the banking use or disclosure.

obligations.provision: Schedule 1, APP 11.1–11.2 ( including APP 11.3 retention commentary )
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Sch 1, Part 4, clauses 11.1–11.2 (APP 11)
obligations.title: Security, retention and destruction of personal information
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APP entity must take reasonable technical and organisational steps to protect personal information it holds from misuse, interference, loss and unauthorised access, modification or disclosure, and must destroy or de-identify it once no longer needed for any permitted purpose and not required by law to be retained.
applicability_conditions: Entity holds personal information in prompts, embeddings, training corpora, logs or outputs
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All banking AI systems storing or processing personal information.
obligations.control_objective: Protect personal information and securely destroy or de-identify it when no longer required.

suggested_questions.security_controls_defined: Are security controls for all personal-information assets used by the AI system documented and implemented?
suggested_questions.retention_schedule_applied: Is an approved retention period applied to prompts, outputs, logs and source data containing personal information?
suggested_questions.destruction_or_deidentification_verified: Is destruction or de-identification verified when personal information is no longer required?

obligations.source_location: Schedule 1, Part 4 — Security of personal information
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Technical feasibility of deleting personal information embedded in trained model weights vs. RAG vector indices requires architectural review.

obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Sch 1, Part 5, clauses 12.1–12.10 and 13.1–13.5 (APP 12 & APP 13)
obligations.title: Access to and correction of personal information in AI workflows
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APP entity that holds personal information about an individual must give the individual access on request within a reasonable period (APP 12) and take reasonable steps to correct inaccurate, out-of-date, incomplete, irrelevant or misleading personal information across relevant records and downstream recipients (APP 13).
applicability_conditions: Entity holds personal information in AI data stores, vector indices, logs or customer profiles
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: Banking AI systems retaining customer profiles, transcripts, vector embeddings or generated case notes.
obligations.control_objective: Enable individuals to access and correct personal information held or generated by the AI system within statutory timeframes.
evidence_requirements: Data store retrieval and correction mechanism

suggested_questions.ai_personal_records_retrievable_for_acce: Can personal information stored in AI logs, vector databases and generated case notes be located and provided for an APP 12 access request?
suggested_questions.correction_propagated_to_ai_stores: When a customer record is corrected under APP 13, is the correction propagated to downstream AI caches, vector stores and context windows?
suggested_questions.access_and_correction_timeframes_tracked: Are access and correction requests involving AI-held records completed within the 30-calendar-day statutory benchmark?

obligations.source_location: Schedule 1, Part 5 — Access to, and correction of, personal information
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Scope of APP 12 exceptions for commercially sensitive evaluative algorithms (APP 12.3(j)) must be separated from the underlying personal information.

obligations.instrument: Privacy Act 1988 / Part IIIC Notifiable Data Breaches
obligations.provision: Part IIIC, ss 26WE–26WL
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Part IIIC, Divisions 1–3, sections 26WE–26WL
obligations.title: Eligible data breach assessment and notification for AI incidents
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: Where unauthorised access to, unauthorised disclosure of, or loss of personal information held by an APP entity occurs (including via prompt injection, model data leakage or vendor breach) and is likely to result in serious harm, the entity must assess suspected breaches expeditiously (within 30 days) and notify the OAIC and affected individuals.
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APP entity holding personal information in the AI system or third-party AI environment
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All banking AI workflows processing personal information.
obligations.control_objective: Detect AI-related personal data leakage, complete Part IIIC serious-harm assessments within 30 days, and notify the OAIC and affected individuals of eligible data breaches.

suggested_questions.ai_data_leakage_detection_enabled: Can the bank detect cross-session or cross-customer personal information leakage in AI prompts, retrieval context and outputs?
suggested_questions.ndb_30day_assessment_workflow_defined: Are suspected AI personal-data breaches routed to Privacy/Legal for a Part IIIC serious-harm assessment within 30 calendar days?
suggested_questions.oaic_and_individual_notification_prepare: Does the incident playbooks cover OAIC and individual notification under s 26WK/26WL including shared third-party AI breaches under s 26WC?

obligations.source_location: Part IIIC — Notification of eligible data breaches
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: None; statutory 30-day assessment expectation (s 26WH(2)) and serious-harm criteria (s 26WG) are explicit.

obligations.provision: Schedule 1, APP 1.7–1.9 (commencing 10 December 2026)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024 (Cth) Sch 1, Part 15, items 94–95 inserting Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Sch 1, clauses 1.7–1.9
obligations.title: Privacy-policy transparency for significant automated decisions
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: Where an entity has arranged for a computer program to make, or do a thing substantially and directly related to making, a decision that could reasonably be expected to significantly affect the rights or interests of an individual and personal information is used in the operation of the program, the APP privacy policy must disclose the kinds of personal information used, the kinds of decisions made, and whether decisions are made solely or substantially assisted by the program.
obligations.version: Privacy and Other Legislation Amendment Act 2024
applicability_conditions: AI computer program uses personal information
Program makes, or does a thing substantially and directly related to making, a decision that could reasonably be expected to significantly affect an individual's rights or interests
Assessment date is on or after 10 December 2026 (conditional prior to commencement)
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: Banking AI systems making or materially assisting credit, hardship, fraud account blocks, claims, pricing or refund decisions.
obligations.control_objective: Disclose prescribed information about significant automated decisions in the APP privacy policy when the amendment applies.

suggested_questions.significant_decision_screened: Has the use case been screened for decisions that could reasonably be expected to significantly affect an individual's rights or interests?
suggested_questions.personal_information_kinds_disclosed: Where APP 1.7 applies, does the privacy policy identify the kinds of personal information used by the automated-decision program?
suggested_questions.decision_kinds_disclosed: Where APP 1.7 applies, does the privacy policy identify the kinds of decisions made or materially assisted by the program?

obligations.source_citation: Privacy Act 1988 (Cth) Sch 1, APP 1.7–1.9 (inserted by C2024A00128 Sch 1 Pt 15)
obligations.source_location: Schedule 1, Part 1, clauses 1.7–1.9
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Future-dated to 10 December 2026 (24 months after Royal Assent on 10 December 2024). Interpretation of 'substantially and directly related' follows OAIC Chapter 1 v2.0 (30 Sep 2026) guidance.
obligations.legal_note: Future-dated at the pack verification date; do not treat as currently in-force before 10 December 2026.

obligations.provision: Chapter 1 (APP 1), paras 1.7–1.18 (v2.0, 30 Sep 2026)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: OAIC Australian Privacy Principles Guidelines, Chapter 1: APP 1, paragraphs 1.7–1.18
obligations.title: Privacy by design and Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) expectations for AI
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: OAIC guidance expects APP entities to embed privacy by design into new technologies and conduct a threshold privacy assessment and Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) for projects involving automated decision-making, novel AI processing, or high privacy risk.
applicability_conditions: AI use case processes personal information
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: APP entities designing or deploying AI systems handling personal information.
obligations.control_objective: Conduct a threshold privacy assessment and Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) prior to deploying AI workflows that handle personal information.

suggested_questions.pia_recommendations_tracked_to_closure: Where a PIA was required, have all privacy risk treatments been signed off and tracked to closure?
suggested_questions.privacy_by_design_controls_embedded: How are privacy-by-design controls embedded into the AI system architecture and data pipeline?

obligations.source_citation: OAIC APP Guidelines Ch 1 (v2.0, 30 Sep 2026), paras 1.7–1.18
obligations.source_location: Chapter 1: APP 1 — Open and transparent management of personal information
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Issued under s 28(1)(a) of the Privacy Act as non-binding supervisory guidance explaining how OAIC assesses APP 1.2 compliance.

obligations.provision: Chapter 3 paras 3.14–3.25; Chapter 6 paras 6.14–6.32; Chapter 10 paras 10.8–10.21
obligations.exact_clause_reference: OAIC Australian Privacy Principles Guidelines, Ch 3 (paras 3.14–3.25), Ch 6 (paras 6.14–6.32) and Ch 10 (paras 10.8–10.21)
obligations.title: Inferred personal information governance and proportional quality verification
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: OAIC guidelines state that generating new personal information by inference, profiling or AI prediction constitutes a 'collection' subject to APP 3 necessity rules, secondary use for AI training requires APP 6 alignment, and APP 10 quality checks must be proportionate to the risk of adverse impact on the individual.
applicability_conditions: AI system generates inferences, profiles, scores or summaries about identifiable individuals
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: Banking AI systems generating customer risk scores, vulnerability indicators, propensity scores or case summaries.
obligations.control_objective: Treat AI-inferred personal attributes as regulated collection under APP 3 and verify inference accuracy proportionately under APP 10.
evidence_requirements: APP 3/6 lawful basis assessment for inferred data

suggested_questions.inferred_attributes_classified_as_collec: Are AI-inferred customer attributes or scores inventoried and assessed as newly collected personal information under APP 3?
suggested_questions.training_data_purpose_compatibility_veri: Has the bank documented the APP 6 basis or de-identification standard before using customer records to train or tune AI models?
suggested_questions.proportional_accuracy_checks_before_cust: Are higher-rigour accuracy and human-verification checks applied when AI inferences can adversely affect a customer?

obligations.source_citation: OAIC APP Guidelines Ch 3 paras 3.14–3.25, Ch 6 paras 6.14–6.32, Ch 10 paras 10.8–10.21
obligations.source_location: Chapters 3, 6 and 10 of the OAIC APP Guidelines
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Non-binding interpretive guidance; however, OAIC applies these interpretations in regulatory investigations and determinations.

obligations.provision: CPS 220 paras 9, 19–22, 26–28 (Risk management framework, RAS and RMS)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 220 Risk Management, paragraphs 9, 19–22, 26–28
obligations.title: AI risk incorporated into the risk management framework
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APRA-regulated institution must maintain a risk management framework (including a Board-approved Risk Appetite Statement and Risk Management Strategy) that identifies, assesses, manages, mitigates and monitors material risks across all operations, with clear risk ownership and Board/senior management oversight.
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APRA-regulated institution (e.g., ADI, insurer, authorised NOHC)
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All APRA-regulated institutions deploying or relying on AI systems.
obligations.control_objective: Identify, assess, manage and oversee material AI risks within the entity's risk management framework.

suggested_questions.ai_risk_identified: Are the material risks created or changed by this AI use case recorded in the bank's risk management framework?
suggested_questions.risk_ownership_assigned: Is an accountable risk owner assigned for each material AI risk?
suggested_questions.risk_controls_monitored: Are the controls for material AI risks subject to defined ongoing monitoring?
suggested_questions.board_or_senior_oversight: Is reporting and escalation to the appropriate senior-management or Board forum defined?

obligations.source_location: CPS 220 Risk Management Framework, Risk Appetite and Risk Management Strategy
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: CPS 220 does not name AI explicitly; AI risks fall under strategic, operational, compliance and conduct material risk categories in para 26.

obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 220 Risk Management, paragraphs 37–47 and 51
obligations.title: Independent review and risk management challenge for AI governance
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APRA-regulated institution must maintain a designated risk management function providing effective challenge, subject its risk management framework to regular appropriateness, effectiveness and comprehensiveness reviews by operationally independent persons, and support the Board's annual Risk Management Declaration.
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APRA-regulated institution
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: Entity-level 2nd and 3rd line assurance functions in APRA-regulated banks.
obligations.control_objective: Ensure independent second-line challenge and third-line audit/comprehensive review cover AI risk management controls.
evidence_requirements: CPS 220 comprehensive review scope and report
CPS 220 Risk Management Declaration attestation pack

suggested_questions.second_line_risk_challenge_recorded: Has the independent risk management function (Line 2) reviewed and challenged the risk assessment for this AI use case?
suggested_questions.independent_framework_review_covers_ai: Are AI risk governance and model/agent controls included within the scope of independent CPS 220 reviews?
suggested_questions.material_ai_control_gaps_escalated_for_d: Are unresolved material AI control deficiencies escalated into the CPS 220 annual Risk Management Declaration process?

obligations.source_location: CPS 220 Risk Management Function, Review of the Risk Management Framework, and Risk Management Declaration
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: None; CPS 220 paras 45–47 mandate comprehensive review at least every three years.

obligations.provision: CPS 230 paras 22–33 (Operational risk management, change assessment and incidents)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 230 Operational Risk Management (Revised 30 April 2026, effective 1 July 2026), paragraphs 22–33
obligations.title: Operational risk controls for the AI service
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APRA-regulated entity must assess the impact of new or changed products, processes and technology on its operational risk profile (para 26), design and test internal controls to mitigate operational risks within appetite (paras 27–30), and identify, escalate and remediate operational incidents and near misses (paras 31–33).
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APRA-regulated entity subject to CPS 230
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All APRA-regulated entities introducing or operating AI technologies.
obligations.control_objective: Manage AI-related operational risk through documented controls, monitoring, incidents and remediation.

suggested_questions.operational_risks_assessed: Has the bank assessed operational risks arising from failure, misuse, model drift and dependency outages for this AI use case?
suggested_questions.control_environment_documented: Are preventive, detective and corrective controls for those operational risks documented with owners?
suggested_questions.incidents_and_weaknesses_managed: Are AI incidents and control weaknesses captured, escalated and tracked to remediation?

obligations.source_citation: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 230 (effective 1 July 2026), paras 22–33
obligations.source_location: CPS 230 Operational risk management — Risk profile, internal controls and incident management
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Core operational risk management clauses (paras 22–33) commenced 1 July 2025 under F2023L01025 and continue in force under the revised 1 July 2026 CPS 230 determination.

obligations.provision: CPS 230 paras 34–47 (Critical operations, tolerance levels and business continuity)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 230 Operational Risk Management (Revised 30 April 2026, effective 1 July 2026), paragraphs 34–47
obligations.title: Continuity for critical operations dependent on AI
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APRA-regulated entity must identify its critical operations (including payments, customer inquiries and core banking processes), set Board-approved tolerance levels (maximum period of disruption, maximum data loss and minimum service levels), and maintain and systematically test a credible Business Continuity Plan (with Non-SFI deferral concluded on 1 July 2026).
obligations.supersedes: AU-APRA-CPS230-BCP@F2023L01025 (effective 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30; Non-SFI BCP transition ended 2026-07-01)
applicability_conditions: Entity is APRA-regulated
AI system supports or is a dependency of a CPS 230 critical operation
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: AI systems supporting critical banking operations (payments, deposit taking, settlements, customer inquiries/complaints, credit management).
obligations.control_objective: Maintain and test continuity arrangements where an AI service supports a critical operation.

suggested_questions.critical_operation_dependency_mapped: Is the AI service mapped to every critical operation and dependent process it supports?
suggested_questions.tolerance_and_fallback_defined: Are disruption tolerances and an executable fallback or manual process defined?
suggested_questions.continuity_plan_tested: Has the continuity arrangement been tested under a realistic AI-service failure scenario?

obligations.source_citation: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 230 (effective 1 July 2026), paras 34–47
obligations.source_location: CPS 230 Business continuity planning — Critical operations, tolerance levels and testing
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Para 36 prescribes baseline critical operations for ADIs (payments, deposit-taking, customer inquiries) unless justified otherwise; Non-SFI BCP transitional deferral expired 1 July 2026.

obligations.provision: CPS 230 paras 48–58 & Attachment (Management of service provider arrangements & NTSP exemptions)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 230 Operational Risk Management (Revised 30 April 2026, effective 1 July 2026), paragraphs 48–58 and Attachment
obligations.title: Third-party AI service provider risk management
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain a Board-approved service provider management policy and register of material service providers, perform due diligence (including fourth-party risk), include mandatory clauses in legally binding agreements (service levels, APRA access, termination, subject to Attachment exemptions for Non-Traditional Service Providers effective 1 July 2026), and monitor performance and exit feasibility across all new and legacy contracts.
obligations.supersedes: AU-APRA-CPS230-SP@F2023L01025 (effective 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30; legacy contract transition ended 2026-07-01)
applicability_conditions: Entity is APRA-regulated
Use case relies on a third-party AI model, platform or service provider assessed as a Material Service Provider under CPS 230 para 49/50
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: APRA-regulated entities contracting external foundation model providers, cloud AI hosts or SaaS AI vendors.
obligations.control_objective: Assess, contract for, monitor and exit material third-party AI service arrangements.

suggested_questions.provider_materiality_assessed: Has the third-party AI provider been assessed for materiality under the bank's CPS 230 framework?
suggested_questions.due_diligence_completed: Does approved due diligence cover the provider's AI, data, security, resilience and subcontractor risks?
suggested_questions.contract_controls_defined: Do binding contract terms cover required controls, incident notification, audit/access rights and data handling?
suggested_questions.performance_and_exit_monitored: Are service performance, control changes and a feasible exit plan monitored and tested?

obligations.source_citation: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 230 (effective 1 July 2026), paras 48–58 & Attachment
obligations.source_location: CPS 230 Management of service provider arrangements and Attachment (NTSP exemptions)
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Materiality classification of foundation-model API providers depends on whether the arrangement supports a critical operation or exposes the bank to material operational risk. Commercial AI model/cloud vendors do not qualify for the 1 July 2026 Non-Traditional Service Provider (NTSP) contractual exemption.

obligations.provision: CPS 230 paras 32–33, 59–60 (APRA notification for operational incidents and material service providers)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 230 Operational Risk Management (Revised 30 April 2026, effective 1 July 2026), paragraphs 32–33 and 59–60
obligations.title: APRA notifications for material operational incidents, MSP agreements and offshoring
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APRA-regulated entity must notify APRA as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a material operational incident (para 33), submit its register of material service providers annually using the updated 1 July 2026 MSP Register template including 'exempt' NTSP classifications where applicable (para 59), notify APRA within 20 business days of entering or materially changing an MSP agreement for a critical operation (para 60(a)), and notify APRA prior to entering into any material offshoring arrangement (para 60(b)).
applicability_conditions: Entity is APRA-regulated
Material operational incident occurs OR entity enters/changes a material service provider or material offshoring AI arrangement
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: APRA-regulated entities engaging material third-party or offshore AI providers.
obligations.control_objective: Screen AI vendor arrangements and operational incidents against CPS 230 72-hour, 20-business-day, annual register and prior-offshoring APRA notification triggers.
evidence_requirements: CPS 230 Material Service Provider Register entry

suggested_questions.msp_register_updated_for_ai_vendors: Is the AI vendor recorded on the bank's CPS 230 Material Service Provider Register where applicable?
suggested_questions.prior_apra_consultation_for_material_off: Where the AI service involves a material offshoring arrangement, was APRA notified prior to entering into or materially changing the arrangement?
suggested_questions.incident_72h_and_agreement_20bd_notifica: Do governance procedures enforce the 20-business-day MSP contract notification and 72-hour material operational incident notification to APRA?

obligations.source_citation: APRA Prudential Standard CPS 230 (effective 1 July 2026), paras 32–33, 59–60
obligations.source_location: CPS 230 Notification requirements (Operational incidents & Service provider arrangements)
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: None; statutory timeframes (72 hours, 20 business days, prior offshoring notice) and the 1 July 2026 updated MSP Register template are explicitly specified in CPS 230.

obligations.provision: CPS 234 paras 13–20 (Roles, responsibilities and information asset classification)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security, paragraphs 13–20
obligations.title: Information security accountability and AI information asset classification
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: The Board of an APRA-regulated entity is ultimately responsible for information security (para 13), must clearly define security roles and responsibilities (paras 14–18), maintain an information security policy framework (para 19), and classify and catalogue all information assets (including those managed by related parties and third parties) by criticality and sensitivity (para 20).
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APRA-regulated entity
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All APRA-regulated entities managing AI prompts, training data, vector databases, model weights and API credentials.
obligations.control_objective: Classify all AI information assets (including prompts, embeddings, weights and third-party hosted assets) by criticality and sensitivity with clear security ownership.

suggested_questions.security_roles_and_asset_owners_assigned: Are information security responsibilities and an accountable asset owner assigned for all AI datasets, models and prompts?
suggested_questions.ai_assets_classified_by_criticality_and_: Have all AI information assets been formally classified by both criticality and sensitivity in accordance with CPS 234 para 20?
suggested_questions.third_party_managed_ai_assets_catalogued: Does the asset classification register include AI information assets hosted or processed by third parties and related entities?

obligations.source_location: CPS 234 Roles and responsibilities, Policy framework, and Information asset identification and classification
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: None; CPS 234 para 20 explicitly applies to assets managed by the entity, related parties and third parties.

obligations.provision: CPS 234 paras 21–26 (Implementation of information security controls)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security, paragraphs 21–26
obligations.title: Commensurate information security controls
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain information security controls commensurate with the vulnerabilities and threats to its information assets, their criticality and sensitivity, and the stage of the asset lifecycle, and must evaluate the design of third-party information security controls where assets are managed by third parties.
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APRA-regulated entity
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All APRA-regulated entities operating internal or third-party AI systems.
obligations.control_objective: Implement security controls commensurate with threats, vulnerabilities, criticality and sensitivity of relevant information assets.

suggested_questions.information_assets_identified: Are all information assets supporting the AI system identified, classified and owned?
suggested_questions.threats_and_vulnerabilities_assessed: Has the bank assessed AI-specific threats and vulnerabilities for those assets?
suggested_questions.controls_commensurate: Are information security controls demonstrably commensurate with the assets' threats, vulnerabilities, criticality and sensitivity?
suggested_questions.third_party_assets_in_scope: Are relevant third-party managed information assets included in the control scope?

obligations.source_location: CPS 234 Implementation of controls
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: AI-specific attack vectors (indirect prompt injection, model inversion, tool-use privilege escalation) must be mapped as threats under para 21(a).

obligations.provision: CPS 234 paras 27–34 (Testing of controls and internal audit)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security, paragraphs 27–34
obligations.title: Systematic testing of information security controls
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APRA-regulated entity must test the effectiveness of its information security controls through a systematic testing program whose scope and frequency are commensurate with threat/vulnerability exposure, asset criticality/sensitivity and material change, and escalate and remediate control deficiencies.
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APRA-regulated entity
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All APRA-regulated entities operating AI systems.
obligations.control_objective: Systematically test information security controls and remediate identified deficiencies.

suggested_questions.testing_program_exists: Has the bank established and executed a testing program for the AI system's relevant information security controls?
suggested_questions.testing_scope_defined: Does the program define the information assets, controls, attack paths and third-party components in scope?
suggested_questions.testing_frequency_risk_based: Is test frequency based on material changes, threats, vulnerabilities, criticality and prior findings?
suggested_questions.testing_results_reviewed: Are test results independently reviewed and reported to the accountable control owners?
suggested_questions.deficiencies_remediated: Are identified deficiencies prioritised, owned, tracked and retested to closure?

obligations.source_location: CPS 234 Testing control effectiveness and Internal audit
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: None; paras 27–31 set explicit criteria for systematic testing.

obligations.provision: CPS 234 paras 32–36 (Incident management and APRA notification)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Standard CPS 234 Information Security, paragraphs 32–36
obligations.title: Information security incident management and notification
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: An APRA-regulated entity must maintain robust detection and response plans for information security incidents, notify APRA as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of a material information security incident (para 35), and notify APRA within 10 business days after becoming aware of a material information security control weakness not remediable in a timely manner (para 36).
applicability_conditions: Entity is an APRA-regulated entity
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: All APRA-regulated entities operating internal or third-party AI systems.
obligations.control_objective: Detect, respond to, escalate and notify material AI-related information security incidents and control weaknesses.

suggested_questions.incident_detection_defined: Are detection signals and thresholds defined for AI-related information security incidents?
suggested_questions.response_and_escalation_defined: Does the incident plan identify containment, escalation, decision and communication responsibilities?
suggested_questions.apra_notification_screened: Is every relevant incident assessed promptly against APRA notification requirements with the rationale recorded?
suggested_questions.material_weaknesses_tracked: Are material information-security control weaknesses assessed, notified where required and tracked to closure?

obligations.source_location: CPS 234 Incident management and APRA notification
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Note CPS 234 para 35 (72 hours for material information security incident) and para 36 (10 business days for material information security control weakness).

obligations.provision: CPG 235 paras 12–19 (Data risk governance, roles and accountability)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: Prudential Practice Guide CPG 235 Managing Data Risk, paragraphs 12–19
obligations.title: Data risk governance, ownership and stewardship for AI
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: APRA guidance expects regulated institutions to manage data risk systematically within their risk management framework, establishing clear data ownership, stewardship, metadata standards and accountability for critical data elements used in business and risk decisions.

obligations.entity_and_business_scope: APRA-regulated entities managing training, retrieval and inference datasets for AI.
obligations.control_objective: Assign data owners, stewards and data quality tolerances for critical data elements supporting the AI system.

suggested_questions.critical_ai_data_elements_owned: Are accountable data owners and stewards assigned for all critical data feeds and corpora used by the AI system?
suggested_questions.data_risk_appetite_and_tolerances_define: Are data quality tolerances (accuracy, completeness, timeliness) defined in alignment with the bank's data risk appetite?
suggested_questions.metadata_and_data_dictionary_maintained: Is a current data dictionary and provenance record maintained for all training, RAG and prompt datasets?

obligations.source_citation: APRA Prudential Practice Guide CPG 235, paras 12–19
obligations.source_location: CPG 235 Governance and managing data risk

applicability_conditions: Entity is an APRA-regulated institution

obligations.control_objective: Maintain end-to-end data lineage, automated ingestion validation, and lifecycle archival/disposal controls for AI data pipelines.

suggested_questions.end_to_end_data_lineage_documented: Is end-to-end data lineage documented from authoritative banking systems through to AI prompts, embeddings and outputs?

suggested_questions.lifecycle_archival_and_disposal_enforced: Are AI training snapshots, embeddings and inference logs archived or disposed of in accordance with CPG 235 lifecycle standards?

obligations.source_citation: APRA Prudential Practice Guide CPG 235, paras 20–45
obligations.source_location: CPG 235 Managing data across its life-cycle and Data validation
obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Non-binding prudential practice guide; supports CPS 220 and CPS 230 operational controls.

obligations.provision: RG 271 paras 271.27–271.32, 271.51–271.68 (Enforceable IDR complaint handling and response)
obligations.exact_clause_reference: ASIC Regulatory Guide 271 Internal dispute resolution, paragraphs 271.27–271.32 and 271.51–271.68 (ASIC Instrument 2020/98)
obligations.title: Recognise, record and respond to complaints fairly and on time
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: A financial firm must recognise any expression of dissatisfaction made to or about the firm where a response or resolution is explicitly or implicitly expected (RG 271.27), record all complaints, handle them fairly and objectively, and provide a compliant written IDR response within 30 calendar days (RG 271.56) including reasons and AFCA escalation details.

AI workflow receives, triages, assists or responds to retail customer complaints or disputes

obligations.control_objective: Identify expressions of dissatisfaction, record them, handle them fairly and issue compliant responses within applicable timeframes.

suggested_questions.complaints_broadly_recognised: Can the AI workflow identify a broad expression of dissatisfaction as a complaint even when the customer does not use the word 'complaint'?
suggested_questions.complaints_recorded: Is every identified complaint recorded in the bank's IDR system with a complete audit trail?
suggested_questions.response_timeframes_enforced: Are applicable RG 271 response timeframes and delay notifications enforced by workflow controls?
suggested_questions.response_content_complete: Does every required written IDR response contain reasons, rights and AFCA information appropriate to the matter?
suggested_questions.human_escalation_available: Can a customer obtain timely human complaint review without the AI treating its own output as final?

obligations.extraction_uncertainty: Shorter timeframes apply to credit hardship/default notice complaints (21 calendar days under RG 271.64).

AI service interacts with retail customers or generates outcomes that can trigger complaints

suggested_questions.systemic_issue_thresholds_defined: Are thresholds and decision rules defined for identifying a systemic issue from AI-related complaints?
suggested_questions.systemic_issues_escalated: Are suspected systemic issues escalated to accountable risk and product owners?
suggested_questions.affected_customers_remediated: Does the process identify and remediate other customers affected by the same AI-related issue?

AI system supports or delivers regulated financial services

suggested_questions.efficient_honest_fair_outcome_tested: Has the AI workflow been tested to ensure customer outcomes remain efficient, honest and fair under s 912A(1)(a)?

Staff or representatives use or supervise the AI system in providing financial services

obligations.control_objective: Train and supervise staff operating AI tools so they understand model limitations and can override erroneous outputs.

suggested_questions.operator_ai_competence_and_training_comp: Are representatives who use or review this AI system trained on its capabilities, limitations and error modes?

obligations.title: Mandatory human approval, pre-execution payment block and audit logging above delegated AUD threshold
obligations.concise_obligation_summary: Any AI-initiated or AI-recommended refund, payment, fee waiver or credit adjustment exceeding the approved enterprise AUD delegated-authority threshold must be blocked from automatic execution until an authorised human officer reviews and approves the action, with immutable approval logs retained for at least seven years.
applicability_conditions: Enterprise internal controls are enabled OR a delegated AUD approval threshold applies to the AI workflow
obligations.entity_and_business_scope: Banking AI agents capable of recommending or executing refunds, payments, waivers or account adjustments.
obligations.control_objective: Enforce deterministic pre-execution human approval gates and 7-year audit log retention for AI financial actions above the enterprise AUD threshold.
